data.body:
AC1/AC2 (exact-patchset CI) + AC5 (live-DC attempt) + AC7 (deletion census) update:

CI wiring (AC1/AC2): added .github/workflows/jira-dc-exact-patchset.yml -
workflow_dispatch-only, dispatched the same way gerrit-verify.yaml is (full
GERRIT_* input set), checks out the exact patchset via the same
checkout-gerrit-change-action pinned commit gerrit-verify.yaml uses, then a new
step does `git rev-parse HEAD` and hard-fails (exit 1) on any mismatch against
`inputs.GERRIT_PATCHSET_REVISION` before recording the verified SHA to
$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY. The live suite runs with REBAR_RUN_EXTERNAL=1, which arms
the existing all-skip canary in tests/external/conftest.py - an all-skipped run
fails the job, satisfying AC1's other half without new canary logic. Added a
config-as-artifact guard test, tests/unit/test_jira_dc_exact_patchset_workflow.py
(6 tests, all passing), asserting these properties directly against the parsed
YAML (dispatch-only + full input set, pinned checkout action, HEAD-vs-revision
check present, REBAR_RUN_EXTERNAL + -m external present, teardown always() set,
native amd64 runner) so a future edit can't silently regress any of them. Also
registered the new workflow's display name in tests/unit/test_workflow_names.py's
locked table (that test's own guard caught the omission). actionlint (all
workflows) is clean; the new file is outside zizmor's scope (release.yml + the
Verified-gate vote path only - this lane isn't part of Verified and isn't
invoked by gerrit-verify.yaml).

Live Jira DC attempt (AC5): made a genuine, bounded (~5 min, not a full hour)
local attempt on this arm64 dev host - `docker compose up -d --build` in
tests/external/live_jira_dc succeeded (image built, container started cleanly),
then polled serverInfo every 30s for 3.5 minutes; the container log was still at
"[INFO] Resolving plugin info, may take a while on the first run." the whole
time, consistent with (and corroborating firsthand) the harness README's own
three separately-measured arm64 attempts (up to 55 minutes, never reaching
"Starting the JIRA Plugin System" even with the correct
-Dproduct.start.timeout property). Did not run a full hour given that this
exact constraint is already measured and documented three times over; tore the
harness down cleanly (docker compose down -v) rather than let it run
unattended. Per AC5's own text ("Portable/default CI remains authoritative when
Docker/DC is unavailable; the live lane is additive evidence"), the portable
shadow corpus (tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/mutate/test_payload_shadow_corpus.py,
test_payload_shadow_effect_spies.py - 36 tests, green post-cutover) is the
authoritative regression oracle for this ticket; the live-DC lane's real
execution now depends on the new CI workflow being dispatched against a native
amd64 GitHub Actions runner (ubuntu-latest), which this session could not do
without pushing the change first - the new workflow is wired and
config-as-artifact tested but has not yet had a live green run recorded. This
mirrors the existing jira-dc-harness/jira-dc-capability-map jobs' own primary
intended home (external-integration.yml's own comment: "GitHub's ubuntu-latest
runners are native x86_64 ... that is the primary intended home for this
harness's acceptance evidence, not a local run on Apple Silicon").

AC7 deletion census (targeted follow-up pass): used Serena find_referencing_symbols
plus grep-for-string-references on the concrete named candidates:
- typed_dispatch._LEAVES / _apply_typed: NOT a deletion target - this is the
  CURRENT, already-modern typed single-mutation dispatch table (unrelated to the
  legacy batch-dict path); still the sole production route for typed Mutation
  dispatch, referenced by applier.py, applier_drift_guard.py, mutation_payloads.py,
  and multiple tests. Kept.
- payload_shadow.py (161 LOC): still genuinely load-bearing - directly imported
  and called (compare_scenario, build_typed_mutation, build_legacy_mutation) by
  test_payload_shadow_corpus.py, the portable shadow-replay regression oracle this
  ticket itself designates as primary evidence. NOT dead; kept. (The route-census
  test's invariant is narrower: payload_shadow must be unreferenced by PRODUCTION
  modules, which it already is post-cutover - it's fine and expected for tests to
  still use it.)
- _mutation_to_batch_dict / MutationShape / applier.py's dual-call-shape ternary:
  re-confirmed load-bearing per the prior comment on this ticket (33 references,
  ~50 dependent tests) - not deletion targets.
- No additional dead "obsolete legacy batch leaves/facades" or "test-only
  compatibility re-exports with no supported consumers" were found beyond the two
  ambiguity-branch simplifications already made in outbound_pass.py/batch_dispatch.py.
  Every named candidate this session inspected turned out to have a genuine,
  non-test-only production consumer or to be the designated regression oracle
  itself. Given the ADR 0107 sequencing's own narrow "Delete" step scope (bare-dict
  Mutation.payload constructors only, already eliminated in outbound_pass.py) and
  the risk of this being the irreversible-deletion story, no further deletions are
  made without a new concrete finding.

Pre-flight status: full tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/ suite (3728 passed, 1 skipped),
python scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py --check (active=39 new=0 increased=0
stale=10 - clean), module sizes all well under the 800 LOC cap (outbound_pass.py
306, batch_dispatch.py 611, applier.py 724). make lint/typecheck/full make test
still to run before push.
